nodes.name: Heavy rain and fog
nodes.desc: Winter rain and summer fog drip keep the forest constantly wet; the Hoh and Quinault valleys are among the rainiest places in the continental US.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Gaps in the tall canopy let light reach the mosses, shrubs and seedlings below.

nodes.name: Forest soil nutrients
nodes.desc: Fallen logs, needles and carcasses break down into nutrients that the trees take up again.

nodes.name: Salmon-borne nitrogen
nodes.desc: Nitrogen from the ocean arrives in spawning salmon and is spread along streams by floods and by animals that carry and eat the carcasses.

nodes.name: Fungi and bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down dead wood, needles and salmon carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Sitka spruce
nodes.desc: A giant conifer of the wet coastal forest. Near spawning streams its foliage draws a share of its nitrogen from salmon carcasses.

nodes.name: Western hemlock
nodes.desc: One of the main canopy conifers of the Olympic rainforest, alongside spruce and Douglas-fir.

nodes.name: Douglas Fir
nodes.desc: A tall canopy conifer; old stands of it provide the nesting habitat northern spotted owls need.

nodes.name: Mosses and ferns
nodes.desc: Mosses coat trunks and branches and ferns carpet the floor in the damp understory.

nodes.name: Salmonberry and devil's club
nodes.desc: Understory shrubs of wet forest; berries feed bears and birds, and the shrubs near salmon streams also take up salmon nitrogen.

nodes.name: Ocean phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Microscopic algae at the base of the ocean food web that feeds young salmon.

nodes.name: Krill and small ocean prey
nodes.desc: Small crustaceans that graze plankton and feed salmon and other fish at sea.

nodes.name: Pacific banana slug
nodes.desc: A large yellow forest slug that eats fungi, plant matter and litter, and helps spread seeds.

nodes.name: Roosevelt elk
nodes.desc: Browses shrubs and grazes grasses, and eats conifer seedlings in winter. Olympic protected much of its range.

nodes.name: Northern flying squirrel
nodes.desc: A nocturnal glider of old forest that eats fungi, lichens and seeds, and is the main prey of the spotted owl.

nodes.name: Pacific salmon
nodes.desc: Grow at sea, then swim up rivers to spawn and die, bringing ocean nutrients into the forest.

nodes.name: American black bear
nodes.desc: Omnivore that eats berries, shoots and insects, and fishes for salmon in the Pacific coast; it also strips bark.

nodes.name: Bald eagle
nodes.desc: In the Pacific Northwest, spawning salmon make up most of its diet from late summer through fall, mostly scavenged carcasses.

nodes.name: Northern spotted owl
nodes.desc: Lives in old-growth forest and eats mostly small mammals, especially flying squirrels; competes with invading barred owls.

nodes.name: Cougar
nodes.desc: The park's top land predator; deer and elk are the main prey of cougars, and it is among the predators of elk.
